subject: meteorology
intro: Meteorology turns the atmosphere into data, and it leads to work forecasting weather, analysing climate risk and teaching the physics of air, storms and seasons.

roles.title: Atmospheric and Space Scientists
roles.what: Investigate atmospheric phenomena and interpret meteorological data gathered by surface and air stations, satellites and radar to prepare reports, forecasts and warnings for the public and specialised users.
roles.where: Observation networks, radiosondes, satellites and radar from unit 7, plus the moisture, fronts and global-circulation units, are the forecasting toolkit, and the severe-weather units feed warning decisions.

roles.title: Climate Change Policy Analysts
roles.what: Research and analyse policy developments related to climate change, and make recommendations for actions such as legislation, awareness campaigns or fundraising approaches.
roles.where: The climate-dynamics unit — ENSO and ocean-atmosphere coupling, monsoons, decadal oscillations and climate extremes — supplies the atmospheric science that climate policy analysis has to get right.

roles.title: Hydrologists
roles.what: Research the distribution, circulation and physical properties of surface and underground waters, studying precipitation and its movement through soil, rivers and aquifers to the ocean and atmosphere.
roles.where: Moisture, clouds and precipitation processes from unit 2 are the front end of the hydrological cycle, and the pressure-and-wind unit explains the storms that drive the floods and droughts hydrologists plan for.

roles.title: Atmospheric, Earth, Marine, and Space Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in the physical sciences other than chemistry and physics, including meteorology, combining teaching with research into the atmosphere and climate.
roles.where: The JetStream arc — atmosphere and energy, clouds and precipitation, cyclones, storms and numerical weather prediction — is a complete teaching sequence for introductory atmospheric science.
